questions.question: Q1. Why does the Beer-Lambert law overestimate light penetration in a heavily pigmented 4D-printed composite?

answers.b: Because it ignores scattering, so the real penetration depth is 2-5x shorter in filled resins.
answers.d: Because it only works at night.

explanations.a: Incorrect - it neglects scattering, not over-counts absorption.
explanations.b: Correct - Beer-Lambert assumes pure absorption; scattering by fillers shortens penetration by 2-5x.
explanations.c: Incorrect - pigments attenuate, not amplify, light.
explanations.d: Incorrect - illumination time of day is irrelevant.

questions.question: Q2. If the UV intensity on an azobenzene sample is doubled, the time to reach 90% trans -> cis conversion:

answers.b: Halves, because conversion time is inversely proportional to intensity.

explanations.a: Incorrect - more light speeds up, not slows, conversion.
explanations.b: Correct - t90 = ln(10)/(k I), so doubling I halves the time.
explanations.c: Incorrect - intensity strongly controls the rate.
explanations.d: Incorrect - the relationship is inverse-linear, not inverse-square.

questions.question: Q3. In NIR photothermal actuation, raising the laser power lets you use a shorter exposure. What is the benefit for spatial resolution?

answers.b: Because d = 2 sqrt(D_th t_exp), a shorter exposure gives a smaller heated zone (sharper resolution).

explanations.a: Incorrect - shorter exposure shrinks, not grows, the blur.
explanations.b: Correct - less time for heat to diffuse means a smaller d and more localised activation.
explanations.c: Incorrect - power sets the heating time and hence the blur.
explanations.d: Incorrect - higher power heats more strongly, it does not cool.

questions.question: Q4. Why are superparamagnetic nanoparticles (<20 nm) preferred over larger ferromagnetic particles for magnetic composites?

answers.b: They do not agglomerate below their blocking temperature, keeping the torque-per-gram high.

explanations.a: Incorrect - cost is not the main reason.
explanations.b: Correct - avoiding dipole-dipole agglomeration preserves dispersion and effective torque.
explanations.c: Incorrect - they are smaller, which is precisely the point.
explanations.d: Incorrect - this is unrelated to optical behaviour.

questions.question: Q5. How does particle agglomeration reduce the actuation performance of a magnetic composite?

answers.a: Clusters increase surface area and spin faster.
answers.b: Clusters have a larger effective volume but lower surface area and rotate less freely in the viscous matrix, so torque per gram drops.

explanations.a: Incorrect - clusters reduce, not increase, free rotation.
explanations.b: Correct - agglomerated clusters deliver less usable torque per gram of magnetic material.
explanations.c: Incorrect - agglomeration is a real, detrimental effect.
explanations.d: Incorrect - it does not raise M_s; it impairs rotation.

questions.question: Q6. A composite with 5 vol% particles needs B_crit = 50 mT to bend 45deg. What happens to B_crit if the loading is reduced to 2 vol%?

answers.b: It increases, because B_crit scales inversely with volume fraction (less magnetic material needs a stronger field).

explanations.a: Incorrect - lowering loading raises, not lowers, the required field.
explanations.b: Correct - with B_crit ~ 1/volume-fraction, a leaner composite needs a stronger field.
explanations.d: Incorrect - a finite, larger field is required.

questions.question: Q7. Why does the coil power needed for wireless actuation rise so steeply with implant depth?

answers.b: Because the field falls off as 1/(R^2+r^2)^(3/2) and is further attenuated by tissue, so much more current (and I^2 R power) is needed.

explanations.a: Incorrect - coil mass is not the cause.
explanations.b: Correct - the steep geometric falloff plus exponential tissue attenuation demand far more power at depth.
explanations.c: Incorrect - this concerns the external coil, not a battery.
explanations.d: Incorrect - tissue attenuates, it does not amplify, the field.

questions.question: Q8. What does the 'crossover depth' identified in the coil-design sub-calc represent?

answers.a: The depth at which the implant stops working.
answers.b: The depth beyond which a battery-powered implant (milliwatts) becomes more practical than wireless coil drive (watts).
answers.c: The depth where tissue becomes transparent.

explanations.a: Incorrect - it is a power-economics threshold, not a failure depth.
explanations.b: Correct - beyond the crossover depth, wireless power demand exceeds the practicality of a battery.
explanations.c: Incorrect - it is unrelated to optical transparency.
explanations.d: Incorrect - it is a depth, not a coil dimension.

questions.question: Q9. Based on the actuation-speed comparison, which mapping of stimulus to application is most appropriate?

answers.a: Magnetic -> implants; photo -> surgical robots; thermal -> microfluidics.
answers.b: Magnetic (ms) -> surgical robots; photo (s) -> microfluidics; thermal (min) -> implants.
answers.c: All three are best for the same application.
answers.d: Thermal -> surgical robots because it is fastest.

explanations.a: Incorrect - this mismatches the speeds to the applications.
explanations.b: Correct - the fastest (magnetic) suits surgical robots, photo suits microfluidics, slow thermal suits implants.
explanations.c: Incorrect - their very different speeds suit different uses.
explanations.d: Incorrect - thermal is the slowest, not the fastest.

questions.question: Q10. The coil sub-calc uses delta ~ 50 mm for tissue penetration. Why must this be treated with caution?

answers.a: Because it is exact for all tissues.
answers.b: Because the penetration depth is frequency- and tissue-specific (e.g. ~60 mm in muscle but only ~20 mm in bone), changing the required power.
answers.c: Because tissue does not attenuate fields.
answers.d: Because 50 mm is always too large.

explanations.a: Incorrect - it is an average, not a universal constant.
explanations.b: Correct - delta varies with tissue type and frequency, so deep or bony targets need very different power.
explanations.c: Incorrect - tissue does attenuate electromagnetic fields.
explanations.d: Incorrect - the value is a reasonable average, just not universal.
